newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says ethanol tax break should be extended.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says ethanol tax break should be extended.

text.p: President Clinton said Thursday he was "disappointed" tax breaks for ethanol were not extended in the budget and tax bills passed by Congress.
"I am very disappointed that the tax incentives for renewable fuels were not extended in this budget agreement," Clinton said in a statement.
"By now, all Americans should be aware of the important role ethanol plays in cleaning our air and in providing economic development for rural America," he said.
He said it was critical to extend tax incentives for ethanol beyond 2000.

"Only by extending these incentives until 2007 will farmers and renewable fuels producers have the certainty they need to invest in new ethanol plants and thus to further expand our domestic renewable fuels industry," he said.
He urged Congress to include a seven-year extension of the renewable fuels tax breaks as part of the reauthorization of the transportation bill.
